## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Check the target project for existing components, layout patterns,and tokens that match the design intent. Reuse what the project already has instead of generating new code from sc… [truncated]

## claude.ai Webflow
Call webflow_guide_tool once to learn available Webflow MCP capabilities before using any other tools. Only call it once per session.

## claude.ai Windsor.ai
This MCP server provides access to the Windsor.ai API, which allows
retrieving analytical data from various data sources such as Facebook, Google Ads, and
more using connectors.

When interacting with this MCP server, follow these steps:

1. Call the "get_connectors" tool to get all available connectors and their connected
   accounts.
2. If a connector the user wants is not yet connected, call
   "get_connector_authorization_url" to get a link they can open in their browser to
   set it up (works for all connector types, OAuth and manual).
3. Call the "get_options" tool to list all available fields, date filters and options
   for a specific connector and accounts.
4. Call the "get_fields" tool to get detailed information about specific fields
   of a given connector. This includes field descriptions, their types and the tables
   they belong to. Fields with "NUMERIC" or "PERCENT" types are metrics, while others
   are dimensions. Metrics will be aggregated depending on the dimensions selected.
5. Call the "get_data" tool to retrieve data from a specific connector by providing
   the connector ID, list of account IDs, list of field IDs, date filter, date range,
   and any options and filters if needed.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.

- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.

Triggers: Supabase products (Database, Auth, Edge Functions, Realtime, Storage, Vectors, Cron, Queues); client libraries and SSR integrations (supabase-js, @supabase/ssr) in Next.js, React, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix; auth issues (login, logout, sessions, JWT, cookies, getSession, getUser, getClaims, RLS); Supabase CLI or MCP server; schema changes, migrations, security audits, Postgres extensions (pg_graphql, pg_cron, pg_vector).

## Report: Agents Page Analysis

### 1. File Paths for the Agents Page/UI

**Frontend:**
- **Main page**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx`
- **Category badge component**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/components/AgentCategoryBadge.tsx`
- **Agent icon component**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/components/AgentIcon.tsx`

**Backend:**
- **API endpoint**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/server.js` (line 809-841)
- **Categories endpoints**: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/server.js` (lines 868-967)

**Types definition:**
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/types.ts` (lines 73-78)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/lib/api.ts` (lines 139-161)

---

### 2. Current Structure — How Agents Are Listed/Rendered

The agents page currently groups agents in **two levels**:

**Level 1: Scope-based grouping** (lines 309-342 in AllAgents.tsx)
- **Global agents** — displayed under a "Global" section with a Globe icon
- **Project agents** — grouped by project name (e.g., "ProjectA", "ProjectB"), each under a FolderOpen icon

**Within each scope group:**
- Agents are rendered as `AgentRow` components (line 314-322 for global, 330-339 for projects)
- Each row displays:
  - Agent icon (colored abstract shape or pixel-art)
  - Agent name and category badge (line 372)
  - Description (line 375)
  - Model type (line 378)
  - Last updated date (line 379)
  - Copy/Move/Delete action buttons (lines 383-386)

**Current rendering flow:**
1. All agents fetched via `getUnifiedAgents()` (line 40)
2. Filtered by search, scope, and category filters (lines 74-80)
3. Global agents separated (line 82)
4. Project agents grouped by `projectName` into a Map (lines 83-88)
5. Rendered in `space-y-6` layout with section headers (line 308)

---

### 3. Agent List Data Source

**Fetched from:**
- **Backend API endpoint**: `GET /api/unified/agents` (server.js line 809)

**Data origin process:**
1. Global agents loaded from: `~/.claude/agents/` directory (line 814)
2. Project agents loaded from: project-specific agent directories (line 820)
3. Both are merged into a flat results array (lines 815-823)
4. Results are sorted by `updatedAt` descending (line 839)

**Data sourcing:**
- Agents are **markdown files** (`.md`) with **YAML frontmatter**
- Parsed by `parseAgent()` function (server.js lines 250-270)
- Uses `gray-matter` library to extract frontmatter and body
- Files listed via `fs.readdirSync()` and directory traversal

---

### 4. Agent Metadata Exists

**Frontmatter fields** (from types.ts lines 14-20 and server.js parseAgent):
```
- name (from frontmatter or filename fallback)
- description (from frontmatter)
- category (from frontmatter.category, defaults to 'uncategorized')
- model (from frontmatter)
- tools (from frontmatter)
- tags (from frontmatter, comma-separated)
- output_template (from frontmatter)
- icon (from frontmatter)
- has_training (from frontmatter)
```

**Key for department grouping:** `frontmatter.category` is already present and used throughout the app.

**Category metadata tracked:**
- Categories endpoint (server.js line 868) returns array of `{ name, count }`
- Categories are either custom (stored in config) or derived from agent frontmatter
- Users can create, rename, and delete categories via API

---

### 5. Existing Grouping/Categorization Logic

**Currently implemented:**
1. **Category filtering** — users can filter by category via pill buttons (line 209-246 in AllAgents.tsx)
2. **Category badge display** — shown inline in each agent row (line 373, via AgentCategoryBadge)
3. **Category management UI** — rename, delete, create categories (CategoryFilterPills component, lines 61-412 in AgentCategoryBadge.tsx)

**Backend category support:**
- `GET /api/categories` — returns all categories with counts (server.js 868-886)
- `POST /api/categories` — creates new category (server.js 889-904)
- `POST /api/categories/rename` — renames category across all agents (server.js 907-938)
- `POST /api/categories/delete` — deletes category, reassigns agents (server.js 941-967)
- Query parameter filtering: `GET /api/unified/agents?category=xyz` (server.js 826-830)

**Pre-defined categories in color system:**
AgentCategoryBadge.tsx lines 9-19 define color mappings for categories:
- `software-factory` (purple)
- `personal` (blue)
- `research` (emerald)
- `client-work` (orange)
- `automation` (cyan)
- `marketing` (pink)
- `devops` (red)
- `design` (indigo)
- `uncategorized` (zinc)

---

### Summary

The project **already has department/category infrastructure** in place. Currently:
- ✅ Categories are defined in agent frontmatter
- ✅ Category data model exists in the type system
- ✅ Backend APIs support category CRUD and filtering
- ✅ Frontend has category filter UI with management panel
- ✅ Category badges are displayed in agent rows
- ✅ Color-coded category system exists

**What's missing for department-based grouping:**
- The **rendering logic doesn't group agents by category**—it only filters by category
- Current display groups by **scope (Global/Project)**, not by **department/category**
- To reorganize, you'd need to change the rendering in AllAgents.tsx to group `filtered` agents by `frontmatter.category` instead of by `scope`

Design an implementation plan for reorganizing the Agents page in /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot to group agents by **department** instead of the current Global/Project scope split.

## Decisions already made by user
1. **Taxonomy: Functional groups** (6 departments):
   - Engineering → Koda, Dato, Vex, Luna, Sage, Riko, Bolt, Hawk
   - Design → Vega
   - Research → Scout, Nova, Atlas, Pulse, Harvest
   - Ops/Strategy → Rex, Arya, Verdict, Orbit, Ledger, Echo
   - HR → Cadence, Roster, Witness, Forge, Tutor, Mira
   - Content/SEO → Quill, Zeph
2. **Hierarchy: Department first, scope as chip.** Top-level sections are departments. Each agent row shows a small [G] (Global) or [P:ProjectName] badge. Scope filter tabs remain but are secondary.
3. **Assignment: Write to frontmatter.** Update each agent's `.md` file `category:` field to the slugified department. One-time migration script.

## Context
- Agents page: [client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx)
- Current rendering splits by scope (Global vs each Project) then lists agents flat within each.
- Category system already exists: badge component at [client/src/components/AgentCategoryBadge.tsx](client/src/components/AgentCategoryBadge.tsx), backend APIs at [src/server.js](src/server.js) lines 843-967 (get/create/rename/delete categories, rewrites frontmatter atomically).
- Existing category colors are defined for keys: software-factory, personal, research, client-work, automation, marketing, devops, design, uncategorized. New department slugs will need color entries — or the existing `EXTRA_COLORS` hash fallback handles unknown slugs.
- Current global agent frontmatter mostly has `category: software-factory` or no category at all. Migration will overwrite.
- Agent files live at ~/.claude/agents/*.md (global) and per-project .claude/agents/*.md.

## What to produce
A concrete plan covering:
1. **Department slug choices** — e.g. `engineering`, `design`, `research`, `ops-strategy`, `hr`, `content-seo`. Justify each (URL-safe, matches existing slug style).
2. **Migration approach** — a one-time script (Node, using gray-matter like server.js does) that reads each agent's markdown file, sets `category` in frontmatter based on filename → department map, writes back atomically. Should be idempotent. Should handle both global (~/.claude/agents/) and project directories. Location: propose `scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs` or similar.
3. **UI changes to AllAgents.tsx**:
   - Replace `globalAgents` + `projectGroups` logic (lines 82-88) with a single `departmentGroups: Map<string, UnifiedAgent[]>`, grouped by `agent.frontmatter?.category`.
   - Keep section rendering pattern (SectionHeader component) but iterate departments in a defined order.

# Group Agents Page by Department

## Context

The Agents page ([client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx)) currently groups agents only by scope — a "Global" section plus one section per project. With ~30 agents all flat-listed under "Global", finding an agent by role is slow. Users have to scan the entire list.

This change reorganizes the page to group by **functional department** (Engineering, Design, Research, Ops/Strategy, HR, Content/SEO) so agents are discoverable by what they do, not just where they live. Scope (Global vs Project) moves to a small inline chip on each row.

The category system is already wired end-to-end: frontmatter `category:` field, backend `/api/categories` CRUD with atomic frontmatter rewrites, a filter pill UI, and a colored badge component. The current gap is that (a) most agents are categorized `software-factory` or blank and (b) the page renders by scope, not category. Both are fixed here.

## Department Taxonomy

| Department | Slug | Agents |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering | `engineering` | koda, dato, vex, luna, sage, riko, bolt, hawk |
| Design | `design` | vega |
| Research | `research` | scout, nova, atlas, pulse, harvest |
| Ops/Strategy | `ops-strategy` | rex, arya, verdict, orbit, ledger, echo |
| HR | `hr` | cadence, roster, witness, forge, tutor, mira |
| Content/SEO | `content-seo` | quill, zeph |

28 agents mapped. Any agent not in the map keeps its existing frontmatter.

## Implementation

### 1. Migration script (new file)

`scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs`

- ESM Node script, reuses `gray-matter` (already a dep).
- `DEPARTMENT_MAP: Record<filename, slug>` with the 28 mappings above.
- Walks `~/.claude/agents/*.md` and every `*/.claude/agents/*.md` under `config.json → projectDirs`.
- For each file: lookup by `path.basename(f, '.md').toLowerCase()`. If mapped and `frontmatter.category !== slug`, atomic-write new frontmatter (`.tmp` + `rename`, matching `atomicWriteText` in [src/server.js:~160](src/server.js)).
- Idempotent: second run reports all `OK`.
- Flags: `--dry-run`, `--verbose`. Summary counts at end.
- Run: `node scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs --dry-run` then without the flag.

### 2. AllAgents.tsx changes

**Imports (lines 3–15):**
- Add `Users` from `lucide-react`.
- Add `getColors, formatCategory` from `../components/AgentCategoryBadge` (already exported, lines 29–38).
- Remove `Globe` if no longer used; keep `FolderOpen` only if still referenced.

**Replace grouping (lines 82–88):**

```tsx
const DEPARTMENT_ORDER = [
  'engineering', 'design', 'research', 'ops-strategy', 'hr', 'content-seo',
] as const

const departmentGroups = new Map<string, UnifiedAgent[]>()
for (const a of filtered) {
  const dept = (a.frontmatter?.category as string | undefined) || 'uncategorized'
  if (!departmentGroups.has(dept)) departmentGroups.set(dept, [])
  departmentGroups.get(dept)!.push(a)
}

const orderedDepartments: string[] = [
  ...DEPARTMENT_ORDER.filter((d) => departmentGroups.has(d)),
  ...[...departmentGroups.keys()]
    .filter((d) => !DEPARTMENT_ORDER.includes(d as typeof DEPARTMENT_ORDER[number]) && d !== 'uncategorized')
    .sort(),
  ...(departmentGroups.has('uncategorized') ? ['uncategorized'] : []),
]
```

**Replace render block (lines 308–343):** single loop over `orderedDepartments`, each rendering a `SectionHeader` (color pulled from `getColors(dept).text`, label from `formatCategory(dept)`, icon `Users`) plus the list of `AgentRow`s.

**Add `ScopeBadge` in `AgentRow` (insert at lines 371–374 inside the name row):**

```tsx
<AgentCategoryBadge category={agent.frontmatter?.category as string} />
<ScopeBadge agent={agent} />
```

**New component (after line 389):** `ScopeBadge` renders `[G]` on zinc background for global, `[P:ProjectName]` on amber for project-scoped, with a tooltip. Fully typed, no `any`.

### 3. AgentCategoryBadge.tsx color entries

Add to `CATEGORY_COLORS` (lines 9–19). `design` and `research` already exist — keep. Add four:

| Slug | Hue |
|---|---|
| `engineering` | sky |
| `ops-strategy` | amber |
| `hr` | rose |
| `content-seo` | lime |

None of these four hues are currently in `CATEGORY_COLORS`. `rose` and `lime` exist in `EXTRA_COLORS` (lines 21–27) — promoting to named entries is fine and overrides the hash fallback for these slugs.

## What's NOT changed

- Backend category APIs in [src/server.js](src/server.js) lines 843–969 — already atomic, already handle frontmatter rewrites. Unchanged.
- `CategoryFilterPills` at [AllAgents.tsx:209-246](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx#L209-L246). After migration, `/api/categories` reports the new department slugs with counts; pills work naturally.
- Scope filter tabs at [AllAgents.tsx:193-205](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx#L193-L205) — still filter across departments. `filtered` already respects them.
- `AgentCategoryBadge` component itself — only gains new color entries.
- Drift banner, create panel, copy/move panel, search — all untouched.

## Critical files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs` | NEW — one-time frontmatter migration |
| [client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx) | Replace scope grouping with department grouping; add `ScopeBadge` |
| [client/src/components/AgentCategoryBadge.tsx](client/src/components/AgentCategoryBadge.tsx) | Add 4 color entries (lines 9–19) |
| [src/server.js](src/server.js) | Reference only (atomic write pattern for the migration script) |
| `config.json` | Read by migration script for `projectDirs` |

## Verification

1. `node scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs --dry-run` — expect 28 `UPDATE` lines, 0 `ERROR`, counts 8/1/5/6/6/2 by department.
2. Run without `--dry-run`. Re-run; expect all `OK` (idempotent).
3. Spot-check 2–3 `.md` files in `~/.claude/agents/` — confirm `category:` field matches the table.
4. Start dev server; open Agents page.
   - Six department sections render in the defined order.
   - Each row shows the department-colored category badge **and** a `[G]` or `[P:ProjectName]` scope chip.
   - Section counts: 8, 1, 5, 6, 6, 2.
5. Click "Engineering" pill in the filter bar → 8 rows, all under the Engineering section.
6. Scope tab "Global" → all 28 still show (they are global). "Project" → empty unless project agents exist.
7. Search "koda" → one row under Engineering.
8. Create a new agent with category `engineering` → appears under Engineering after refetch.
9. `cd client && npm run build` — zero TS errors, no `any`.

# Group Agents Page by Department

## Context

The Agents page ([client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx)) currently groups agents only by scope — a "Global" section plus one section per project. With ~30 agents all flat-listed under "Global", finding an agent by role is slow. Users have to scan the entire list.

This change reorganizes the page to group by **functional department** (Engineering, Design, Research, Ops/Strategy, HR, Content/SEO) so agents are discoverable by what they do, not just where they live. Scope (Global vs Project) moves to a small inline chip on each row.

The category system is already wired end-to-end: frontmatter `category:` field, backend `/api/categories` CRUD with atomic frontmatter rewrites, a filter pill UI, and a colored badge component. | Ops/Strategy | `ops-strategy` | rex, arya, verdict, orbit, ledger, echo |

content.text:
Key fixes:
1. **`<button>` → `<div role="button">`** — `draggable` on a native `<button>` is flaky in Chromium; drag rarely starts, and drop handlers don't always fire. Generic elements work reliably.
2. **`pointer-events-none` on the inner `<span>`** — prevents child nodes from becoming the drag target and breaking `dragleave`/`drop` coordination (a classic HTML5 DnD bug where hovering a text node fires leave on the container).
3. **`onDragEnter` added** — some browsers only register the drop target on enter, not first `dragover`.
4. **`dragleave` now ignores enters into its own children** (via `relatedTarget` check) — otherwise the ring flickers and can drop at the wrong moment.
5. **`select-none`** — stops text-selection from hijacking the drag start.
6. **`onClick` guarded by `!dragCat`** — no accidental filter change if a drag ends on the origin pill.

Where does agent "level" / "rank" / "status" / "tier" come from today? **Backend Data Model (SQLite + HR system):** 1. **Core agent fields** (`src/db.js`, lines 187-216): - `level` (INTEGER, default 0) — computed level 0-8 - `levelTitle` (TEXT) — e.g., "Junior", "Senior", "Principal" - `yearsOfExperience` (REAL, default 0) — computed YoE score - `experiencePoints` (REAL) — raw experience points - `progressToNext` (REAL) — progress toward next level - `status` (TEXT, default 'active') — 'active', 'probation', 'pip', 'retired' - `tier` (TEXT, default 'engineer') — 'engineer', 'leadership', 'analyst', 'creative' - `title` (TEXT) — job title, e.g., "Agent", "Commander" - `lastPromoted` (TEXT) — timestamp of last promotion - `pip` (TEXT) — Performance Improvement Plan notes if any 2. **Experience computation** (`src/experience.js`): - Lines 63-80: **LEVEL_THRESHOLDS** (9 levels: Trainee→Fellow) - Level 0: Trainee (0-1 YoE) - Level 1: Junior (1-3 YoE) - Level 2: Mid (3-5 YoE) - Level 3: Senior (5-8 YoE) - Level 4: Lead (8-12 YoE) - Level 5: Principal (12-18 YoE) - Level 6: Staff (18-25 YoE) - Level 7: Distinguished (25-40 YoE) - Level 8: Fellow (40+ YoE) - Lines 41-48: **Weights** (tunable): - trainingKbPerYear: 10 KB .md = 1 YoE - runsPerYear: 20 runs = 1 YoE - daysPerYear: 90 tenure days = 1 YoE - patternWeight: +0.5 per good pattern contributed - antipatternPenalty: -0.3 per antipattern triggered - successBonus: +0.5 for high success rate 3. **Org Registry** (`src/org.js`): - Lines 86-117: **Registry storage** in SQLite (formerly `~/.claude/org/registry.json`) - Per-agent fields: `department`, `phase`, `reportsTo`, `title`, `tier`, `status`, `level`, `levelTitle`, `yearsOfExperience` - Upserted via `/api/org/agent/:id` PATCH endpoint (`src/server.js`, lines 3763-3777) - Allowed fields: `department`, `phase`, `reportsTo`, `title`, `tier`, `status` 4. **HR Module** (`src/hr.js`): - Manages weekly reviews, training queue, capability gaps, antipattern signatures - Stores witness logs, daily scores, recommendations for PIP/promotion ### B. Agent description on /agents page **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx` **Component:** `AgentRow()` function, lines 385-416 **Description rendering:** Line 402 ```tsx

{agent.description}

``` **CSS properties:** - `text-[11px]` — small font size - `text-text-muted` — muted text color - `truncate` — single line, ellipsis on overflow - `mt-0.5` — small top margin The description comes directly from `agent.description` (frontmatter's description field). It's already truncated to 1 line by CSS. To shorten the display further, you'd need to truncate at character level (e.g., first 80 chars + "…"). ### C. Leadership concept **Existing structure in OrgChart** (`client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx`): 1. **Department head concept** (line 225 in org.js): - Departments table has a `head` field (TEXT) — agent ID of the department head - Exposed in API: `OrgChartDepartment.head: string` (line 610 in api.ts) - Used in layout (line 169 in OrgChart.tsx): `head: d.head` - Sorting logic (lines 172-178 in OrgChart.tsx): ``` if (a.id === d.head) return -1 // Head first ``` 2. **Tier-based leadership** (line 184-185 in OrgChart.tsx): - `tier: 'leadership'` agents are rendered as top-level leaders - Can have no `reportsTo` (line 146): `const leaders = allNodes.filter(n => !n.reportsTo)` 3. **Is it structured data?** - YES. Department `head` is a structured field in the database - But agents are NOT enforced to have a `leader` flag in their markdown frontmatter - This is purely org-registry data (SQLite), not markdown metadata ### D. Experience data sources **Current system:** 1. **Experience fields exposed via API** (`src/server.js`, lines 3798-3806): - `/api/experience/:agent` returns the full agent record including: - `yearsOfExperience` (REAL) - `level` (INTEGER, 0-8) - `levelTitle` (TEXT) - `experiencePoints` (REAL) - `progressToNext` (REAL) 2. **Nightly compute** (`src/server.js`, lines 3710-3723): - Server initializes experience on startup by calling `experience.recomputeAllExperience(org)` - On-demand recompute via `/api/experience/recompute` POST 3. **No deprecated registry.json migration needed** — already using SQLite agents table ### E. Agent markdown frontmatter fields **Current frontmatter** (`client/src/types.ts`, lines 14-20): ```typescript export interface AgentFrontmatter { category?: string // dept/category (added recently) tags?: string output_template?: string icon?: string has_training?: boolean } ``` **NOT in markdown frontmatter (stored in registry/org only):** - level, levelTitle, yearsOfExperience - tier, title, status - reportsTo, department, phase - leadership/leader flag ### F. Org Chart page **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx` **Data flow:** 1. Fetches `/api/org-chart` → returns `OrgChartData` (nodes, edges, phases, departments, stats) 2. Departments have `.head` field (agent ID of leader) 3. Sorting in department columns (lines 172-178): - Department head first - Leaders (tier='leadership') next - Then by level (descending) - Then by name 4. Top leaders (tier='leadership' with no reportsTo) rendered separately above departments **Current rendering of agent info in departments:** - MemberInfo (lines 78-92): id, name, emoji, title, model, tier, level, levelTitle, yearsOfExperience, status - No "leadership" badge on individual agents currently visible --- ## Summary: Data Model Decision **Recommendation:** Use **approach (c) — both with fallback**: 1. **Add to agent markdown frontmatter** (new optional fields): - `level: 2` (INTEGER, overrides computed) - `experience_years: 3.5` (REAL, overrides computed) - `leadership: true` (BOOLEAN, marks agent as potential leader candidate) 2. **Fall back to SQLite registry** (computed automatically): - If frontmatter missing, use values from agents table - Experience module continuously updates table nightly - Registry fields (`tier`, `status`, `department`, `reportsTo`, `phase`) stay org-only 3. **Department leader enforcement**: - Each department's `head` field must reference an existing agent - Add validation on update: `/api/org/agent/:id` PATCH should validate `department_id` has exactly one `head` set - Or add a new endpoint `/api/departments/:id/set-head/:agent-id` This keeps the system scalable: experience auto-computes, but editors can override for special cases or onboarding before metrics accumulate.

# Group Agents Page by Department

## Context

The Agents page ([client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx)) currently groups agents only by scope — a "Global" section plus one section per project. With ~30 agents all flat-listed under "Global", finding an agent by role is slow. Users have to scan the entire list.

This change reorganizes the page to group by **functional department** (Engineering, Design, Research, Ops/Strategy, HR, Content/SEO) so agents are discoverable by what they do, not just where they live. Scope (Global vs Project) moves to a small inline chip on each row.

The category system is already wired end-to-end: frontmatter `category:` field, backend `/api/categories` CRUD with atomic frontmatter rewrites, a filter pill UI, and a colored badge component. The current gap is that (a) most agents are categorized `software-factory` or blank and (b) the page renders by scope, not category. Both are fixed here.

## Department Taxonomy

| Department | Slug | Agents |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering | `engineering` | koda, dato, vex, luna, sage, riko, bolt, hawk |
| Design | `design` | vega |
| Research | `research` | scout, nova, atlas, pulse, harvest |
| Ops/Strategy | `ops-strategy` | rex, arya, verdict, orbit, ledger, echo |
| HR | `hr` | cadence, roster, witness, forge, tutor, mira |
| Content/SEO | `content-seo` | quill, zeph |

28 agents mapped. Any agent not in the map keeps its existing frontmatter.

## Implementation

### 1. Migration script (new file)

`scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs`

- ESM Node script, reuses `gray-matter` (already a dep).
- `DEPARTMENT_MAP: Record<filename, slug>` with the 28 mappings above.
- Walks `~/.claude/agents/*.md` and every `*/.claude/agents/*.md` under `config.json → projectDirs`.
- For each file: lookup by `path.basename(f, '.md').toLowerCase()`. If mapped and `frontmatter.category !== slug`, atomic-write new frontmatter (`.tmp` + `rename`, matching `atomicWriteText` in [src/server.js:~160](src/server.js)).
- Idempotent: second run reports all `OK`.
- Flags: `--dry-run`, `--verbose`. Summary counts at end.
- Run: `node scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs --dry-run` then without the flag.

### 2. AllAgents.tsx changes

**Imports (lines 3–15):**
- Add `Users` from `lucide-react`.
- Add `getColors, formatCategory` from `../components/AgentCategoryBadge` (already exported, lines 29–38).
- Remove `Globe` if no longer used; keep `FolderOpen` only if still referenced.

**Replace grouping (lines 82–88):**

```tsx
const DEPARTMENT_ORDER = [
  'engineering', 'design', 'research', 'ops-strategy', 'hr', 'content-seo',
] as const

const departmentGroups = new Map<string, UnifiedAgent[]>()
for (const a of filtered) {
  const dept = (a.frontmatter?.category as string | undefined) || 'uncategorized'
  if (!departmentGroups.has(dept)) departmentGroups.set(dept, [])
  departmentGroups.get(dept)!.push(a)
}

const orderedDepartments: string[] = [
  ...DEPARTMENT_ORDER.filter((d) => departmentGroups.has(d)),
  ...[...departmentGroups.keys()]
    .filter((d) => !DEPARTMENT_ORDER.includes(d as typeof DEPARTMENT_ORDER[number]) && d !== 'uncategorized')
    .sort(),
  ...(departmentGroups.has('uncategorized') ? ['uncategorized'] : []),
]
```

**Replace render block (lines 308–343):** single loop over `orderedDepartments`, each rendering a `SectionHeader` (color pulled from `getColors(dept).text`, label from `formatCategory(dept)`, icon `Users`) plus the list of `AgentRow`s.

**Add `ScopeBadge` in `AgentRow` (insert at lines 371–374 inside the name row):**

```tsx
<AgentCategoryBadge category={agent.frontmatter?.category as string} />
<ScopeBadge agent={agent} />
```

**New component (after line 389):** `ScopeBadge` renders `[G]` on zinc background for global, `[P:ProjectName]` on amber for project-scoped, with a tooltip. Fully typed, no `any`.

### 3. AgentCategoryBadge.tsx color entries

Add to `CATEGORY_COLORS` (lines 9–19). `design` and `research` already exist — keep. Add four:

| Slug | Hue |
|---|---|
| `engineering` | sky |
| `ops-strategy` | amber |
| `hr` | rose |
| `content-seo` | lime |

None of these four hues are currently in `CATEGORY_COLORS`. `rose` and `lime` exist in `EXTRA_COLORS` (lines 21–27) — promoting to named entries is fine and overrides the hash fallback for these slugs.

## What's NOT changed

- Backend category APIs in [src/server.js](src/server.js) lines 843–969 — already atomic, already handle frontmatter rewrites. Unchanged.
- `CategoryFilterPills` at [AllAgents.tsx:209-246](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx#L209-L246). After migration, `/api/categories` reports the new department slugs with counts; pills work naturally.
- Scope filter tabs at [AllAgents.tsx:193-205](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx#L193-L205) — still filter across departments. `filtered` already respects them.
- `AgentCategoryBadge` component itself — only gains new color entries.
- Drift banner, create panel, copy/move panel, search — all untouched.

## Critical files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs` | NEW — one-time frontmatter migration |
| [client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx) | Replace scope grouping with department grouping; add `ScopeBadge` |
| [client/src/components/AgentCategoryBadge.tsx](client/src/components/AgentCategoryBadge.tsx) | Add 4 color entries (lines 9–19) |
| [src/server.js](src/server.js) | Reference only (atomic write pattern for the migration script) |
| `config.json` | Read by migration script for `projectDirs` |

## Verification

1. `node scripts/migrate-agent-departments.mjs --dry-run` — expect 28 `UPDATE` lines, 0 `ERROR`, counts 8/1/5/6/6/2 by department.
2. Run without `--dry-run`. Re-run; expect all `OK` (idempotent).
3. Spot-check 2–3 `.md` files in `~/.claude/agents/` — confirm `category:` field matches the table.
4. Start dev server; open Agents page.
   - Six department sections render in the defined order.
   - Each row shows the department-colored category badge **and** a `[G]` or `[P:ProjectName]` scope chip.
   - Section counts: 8, 1, 5, 6, 6, 2.
5. Click "Engineering" pill in the filter bar → 8 rows, all under the Engineering section.
6. Scope tab "Global" → all 28 still show (they are global). "Project" → empty unless project agents exist.
7. Search "koda" → one row under Engineering.
8. Create a new agent with category `engineering` → appears under Engineering after refetch.
9. `cd client && npm run build` — zero TS errors, no `any`.

---

# Agent Context-Compactor — 4-Phase Plan

**Diagnosis.** 28 agents × ~60KB = ~1.7MB of preamble per SDK run. Koda alone is 192KB / 5,206 lines. Claude Agent SDK loads the agent `.md` body into the system prompt at dispatch — that body **must shrink**. The SDK cannot "lazy load" at runtime, but the *LLM reading the body can* — if the body instructs it to call `Read` on a skill file when keywords trigger. That's the lever.

**Impact ranking (biggest win first):** Phase 1 (core+skills split) recovers ~70% of tokens for power agents with zero server work. Phase 2 (lazy list endpoint) recovers ~80% of the list-page preamble. Phase 3 (pre-write hook) prevents regression. Phase 4 (golden tests) is insurance.

**Core design decision: deterministic script, not LLM.** Phase 1 compactor is a Node script — zero token cost, deterministic, testable, reversible via git. LLM-assisted refinement is deferred to an optional Phase 4 pass. Running an LLM compactor on 28 agents would cost more than it saves for the first 90 days. Validate by running deterministic first, measure drift, only escalate to LLM if heuristics plateau.

---

## Skill-reference syntax (the contract the LLM reads)

In the core body, bottom section, fixed block the LLM is trained to action:

```markdown
## Skill Library (load on demand)
When the user's task mentions keywords in the `triggers` list below, FIRST call
`Read` on the corresponding skill file, THEN proceed. Do not guess — load it.

- billing, subscription, stripe, checkout → ~/.claude/skills/koda/billing.md
- auth, login, session, rls, supabase auth → ~/.claude/skills/koda/auth.md
- migration, schema, rls policy, trigger → (DELEGATE to Dato, do not load)
- debugging, error loop, fix-verify → ~/.claude/skills/koda/debug-protocol.md
```

Frontmatter manifest (machine-readable, used by hook + tests):

```yaml
skills:
  - id: billing
    path: skills/koda/billing.md
    triggers: [billing, subscription, stripe, checkout, pricing]
    lines: 412
  - id: auth
    path: skills/koda/auth.md
    triggers: [auth, login, session, rls]
    lines: 287
compactor:
  version: 1
  budget_lines: 400
  budget_chars: 16000
  last_compacted: 2026-04-15T00:00:00Z
  original_sha: <sha of pre-compact body>
```

**Why this works:** the SDK loads only the ~400-line core containing the trigger block. The model, seeing the block, treats it as executable routing — just like current "MANDATORY: read memory/X" blocks which demonstrably work. No SDK change required.

---

## Budget

| Agent class | Budget (lines) | Chars | Est. tokens | Override |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | 400 | 16,000 | ~4,500 | — |
| Orchestrator (Rex, Arya) | 700 | 28,000 | ~7,500 | `budget_lines: 700` in FM |
| Lightweight (Vex, Zeph) | 300 | 12,000 | ~3,200 | — |

Over-budget = `body_lines > budget_lines` OR `body_chars > budget_chars`. Hook warns at 90%, rejects at 110% unless `compactor.allow_oversize: true`.

---

## PHASE 1 — Deterministic core+skills splitter (ship day 1-2)

**Goal.** Convert Koda + Rex + Riko + Luna (the 4 worst offenders, ~50% of total tokens) into core + skills. **Estimated savings: 60–75% per hot agent, ~40% of total agent-preamble tokens across the roster.**

**Files to create:**
- `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` — CLI: `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs <agent.md> [--write] [--staging]`
- `scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs` — split rules (below)
- `scripts/compactor/render.mjs` — emits core body + skill files + updated frontmatter
- `~/.claude/skills/<agent>/*.md` — output skills (gitignored from repo, but git-tracked in `~/.claude`)
- `scripts/compactor/README.md` — one-pager

**Files to modify:** none in phase 1 (script is standalone; writes via existing `atomicWriteText` imported from `src/server.js` is overkill — use plain `fs.writeFileSync` with `.tmp` + rename).

**Heuristics (apply in order, stop when body ≤ budget):**

1. **H1 — Fenced "on-demand" sections.** Any `## Section` whose heading matches `/^##\s+(billing|auth|migration|testing|deployment|debugging|design|stack-[a-z]+)/i` → extract to `skills/<agent>/<slug>.md`. Triggers = heading words + first-paragraph nouns.
2. **H2 — Pre-build protocol bloat.** Sections titled "DEEP PRE-BUILD PROTOCOL", "PROTOCOL", "CHECKLIST" > 100 lines → extract to `skills/<agent>/protocol.md`. Keep a 5-line summary + pointer in core.
3. **H3 — Example blocks.** Any ```` ``` ```` fenced block > 40 lines → move to `skills/<agent>/examples/<sha8>.md`. Replace with 2-line stub: *"See example: skills/koda/examples/x.md (trigger: <keywords>)"*.
4. **H4 — Tool-specific guidance.** Subsections matching `/^###\s+(Shopify|Supabase|Next\.?js|Stripe|Flutter|iOS)/i` → group by tool into `skills/<agent>/tools/<tool>.md`.
5. **H5 — Pattern catalogs.** Lists of 10+ numbered bullet patterns → move to `skills/<agent>/patterns.md`.
6. **H6 — Anti-pattern / FAQ / appendix.** Sections after `## Appendix`, `## FAQ`, `## Antipatterns` → `skills/<agent>/reference.md`.

**Always preserve in core:** frontmatter, `## Your Role`, `## Tier 1 first-load` (the critical 4-file mandatory list), handoff contracts, skill library block.

**Data shapes.** Frontmatter gains `skills[]` and `compactor{}` as shown above. Nothing else changes — the SDK ignores unknown keys.

**Verification:**
- `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ~/.claude/agents/koda.md --dry-run` → prints before/after line count, skill plan
- Manual eyeball of `--staging` output in `./.compactor-staging/`
- `wc -l ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` must show ≤ 400 after `--write`
- Run one real Koda task against old and new side-by-side, compare output for regression
- Success metric: `du -sh ~/.claude/agents` drops from ~1.7MB to ~600KB

**Rollback.** `cp agent-versions/koda/<ts>.md ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` — existing snapshot system already covers this. Also: git restore in `~/.claude`.

**Risk flags:**
- Heuristic H3 may break trigger phrases that live inside example blocks. **Mitigation:** index first 2 lines of every moved block as triggers automatically.
- Rex is an orchestrator; splitting its dispatch logic breaks everything. **Flag:** Rex gets `budget_lines: 700` and H1/H5 only — never H2/H3.
- User currently has MEMORY.md "MANDATORY" blocks inside agents. Do NOT touch those in phase 1.

---

## PHASE 2 — Server lazy-load + frontmatter-only list (ship day 3)

**Goal.** Stop shipping full agent bodies to the Polyglot UI on the agents list page. **Estimated savings: ~85% of the `/api/global/agents` payload** (1.7MB → ~150KB). Indirectly reduces any LLM that scrapes the Polyglot API for agent discovery.

**Files to modify:**
- `src/server.js` lines 250-270 (`parseAgent`) — add `parseAgentMeta(filePath)` that skips body
- `src/server.js` lines 272-282 (`listAgents`) — add `listAgentsMeta(dir)` variant
- `src/server.js` lines 496-499 (`GET /api/global/agents`) — return meta only; add `?full=1` escape hatch for backcompat
- `src/server.js` lines 501-505 (`GET /api/global/agents/:name`) — add in-process cache wrapper
- `client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx` — if it reads `.body`, switch to fetching detail on expand (grep shows it doesn't hit these endpoints directly — low risk)

**Cache layer (in-process Map, no Redis).** Redis is overkill — agents are <200KB, 28 total, read-hot. A `Map<path, {mtime, parsed}>` keyed by absolute path, invalidated when `fs.statSync(path).mtimeMs !== cached.mtime`. Invalidate on the existing PUT handler at line 507-518 after `atomicWriteText`. Redis adds a network hop + dependency; the whole corpus fits in 2MB RAM. **Decision: Map. If you ever run Polyglot multi-process, revisit.**

```js
const agentCache = new Map();
function parseAgentCached(filePath) {
  const stat = fs.statSync(filePath);
  const hit = agentCache.get(filePath);
  if (hit && hit.mtimeMs === stat.mtimeMs) return hit.parsed;
  const parsed = parseAgent(filePath);
  agentCache.set(filePath, { mtimeMs: stat.mtimeMs, parsed });
  return parsed;
}
// Invalidate in PUT handler (line ~517):
agentCache.delete(filePath);
```

**API shapes:**

```
GET /api/global/agents            → [{ filename, name, description, model, tools,
                                        category, department, lines, skills: [{id,triggers}],
                                        updatedAt }]   // no body, no raw
GET /api/global/agents/:name      → full shape (as today)  — cached
GET /api/global/agents/:name?meta=1 → meta only
```

Backcompat: keep `GET /api/global/agents?full=1` returning today's shape for 30 days; log a deprecation warning.

**Verification:** `curl -s localhost:PORT/api/global/agents | wc -c` before/after. Time list-page load in devtools.

**Rollback.** One-line revert on the list handler — cache is additive.

**Risk:** frontend may destructure `.body` somewhere. Grep `client/src` for `\.body` before merging. (My check showed AllAgents doesn't — safe.)

---

## PHASE 3 — Pre-write hook: guardrail on save (ship day 4)

**Goal.** When any agent `.md` is saved (via PUT or file-watcher), block/warn if over budget. Auto-suggest compaction. **Savings: prevents drift back to bloat.**

**Files to create:**
- `src/compactor/budget.js` — exports `checkBudget(agentObj)` returning `{ok, violations, suggest}`
- `src/compactor/hook.js` — wraps PUT handler

**Files to modify:**
- `src/server.js` lines 507-518 (`PUT /api/global/agents/:name`) — insert budget check pre-write. On violation: return `409 {error, budget, actual, suggestion}` unless body has `?force=1`. Keep atomic write + snapshot logic.

**Behavior:**
- At 90% budget → `200 {ok:true, warning}`
- At 110% budget → `409 {error:"over_budget", runCompactor:"node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ..."}`
- With `?force=1` → write anyway, set `compactor.allow_oversize: true` in FM

**Verification:** PUT a 5000-line body → expect 409. PUT with `?force=1` → expect 200 and FM updated.

**Rollback.** Feature-flag via `POLYGLOT_BUDGET_ENFORCE=0` env var.

**Risk:** user saves legit 500-line orchestrator and gets blocked. Mitigation: the per-agent `budget_lines` override. Keep threshold generous and warn before reject.

---

## PHASE 4 — Golden-prompt regression harness (ship day 5-6)

**Goal.** Prove the compactor didn't make agents dumber. **Savings: none directly — this is the safety net that lets you compact aggressively.**

**v1 (ship now) — diff + manual approve.** Staging-path write, human review. 80/20.
**v2 (defer) — automated LLM-judge scoring.** Only build if v1 reveals frequent regressions.

**Files to create:**
- `tests/golden/<agent>/prompts.json` — 5–10 prompts per hot agent (Koda, Rex, Dato)
  ```json
  [{"id":"billing-checkout","prompt":"Add Stripe checkout to /pricing","expect_keywords":["stripe","webhook","price_id","success_url"],"must_mention_skill":"billing"}]
  ```
- `scripts/compactor/golden-run.mjs` — runs each prompt against OLD and NEW agent body, compares
- `scripts/compactor/score.mjs` — scoring

**Drift metric (v1, cheap).**
1. **Keyword recall** — `expect_keywords` present in response: must be ≥90% of old agent's recall.
2. **Skill-load check** — if prompt should trigger skill X, new response must `Read` that path (grep the tool-call log).
3. **Response length ratio** — new / old in [0.6, 1.4]. Outside → flag.
4. **No embedding similarity in v1.** Too expensive, too fuzzy, not worth it until you have a regression.

**Pass threshold:** all 3 gates green on ≥80% of prompts per agent. Fail → staging file stays, real file untouched, diff rendered to `./.compactor-staging/<agent>.diff.html`.

**Files to modify:** add `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --with-golden` flag that runs the harness before writing.

**Verification:** run against already-compacted Koda; expect all green. Intentionally break a skill trigger; expect red.

**Rollback.** Golden tests are read-only; nothing to roll back. Disable by not passing `--with-golden`.

**Risk flags:**
- Running golden prompts costs real Claude tokens. **Mitigation:** cache OLD responses forever (body hash → response), only re-run NEW. Expected one-time cost: ~$2-5 per hot agent, then $0 for subsequent compactions of the same agent.
- Flaky LLM outputs. **Mitigation:** temperature=0, run NEW twice, require both to pass.

---

## Sequencing & go/no-go

| Day | Phase | Expected tokens saved | Reversible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | P1 on Koda + Rex only | ~30% global | yes (git) |
| 2 | P1 on remaining 26 | +15% global | yes |
| 3 | P2 server lazy-load | +85% list API | trivial |
| 4 | P3 pre-write hook | prevents regression | env flag |
| 5-6 | P4 golden tests | confidence | additive |

**Stop conditions.** If P1 on Koda regresses real tasks (measured by you re-running 3 real prompts), halt, fix heuristics, don't touch other agents. Budget 1 day for tuning heuristics after Koda.

**Anti-over-engineering calls I made:**
- No Redis (Map is fine)
- No LLM compactor in v1 (deterministic)
- No embedding similarity in v1 (keywords)
- No MEMORY.md refactor (deferred, user explicitly said "phase later")
- No DB schema change (frontmatter YAML is enough)
- Kept existing versioning system; didn't replace it

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/server.js
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/scripts/compactor/compact.mjs (new)
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs (new)
- /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/koda.md
- /Users/yashbaldha/.claude/agents/rex.md

**Impact ranking:** P1 (core+skills split) recovers ~70% per hot agent. P2 (server lazy-list) cuts the `/api/global/agents` payload by ~85%. P3 (pre-write hook) prevents regression. P4 (golden tests) is insurance that lets P1 run aggressively.

## Skill-reference syntax (the contract the LLM reads)

Inserted at the bottom of every compacted core body:

```markdown
## Skill Library (load on demand)
When the user's task mentions keywords in the `triggers` list below, FIRST call
`Read` on the corresponding skill file, THEN proceed. Do not guess — load it.

- billing, subscription, stripe, checkout → ~/.claude/skills/koda/billing.md
- auth, login, session, rls → ~/.claude/skills/koda/auth.md
- migration, schema, rls policy → (DELEGATE to Dato, do not load)
- debugging, error loop → ~/.claude/skills/koda/debug-protocol.md
```

Machine-readable manifest in frontmatter (used by hook + tests, ignored by SDK):

```yaml
skills:
  - id: billing
    path: skills/koda/billing.md
    triggers: [billing, subscription, stripe, checkout, pricing]
    lines: 412
  - id: auth
    path: skills/koda/auth.md
    triggers: [auth, login, session, rls]
    lines: 287
compactor:
  version: 1
  budget_lines: 400
  budget_chars: 16000
  last_compacted: 2026-04-15T00:00:00Z
  original_sha: <sha of pre-compact body>
```

## Budget

| Agent class | Budget (lines) | Chars | Est. tokens | Override |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | 400 | 16,000 | ~4,500 | — |
| Orchestrator (Rex, Arya) | 700 | 28,000 | ~7,500 | `budget_lines: 700` |
| Lightweight (Vex, Zeph) | 300 | 12,000 | ~3,200 | — |

Over-budget = `body_lines > budget_lines` OR `body_chars > budget_chars`. Hook warns at 90%, rejects at 110% unless FM has `compactor.allow_oversize: true`.

## PHASE 1 — Deterministic core+skills splitter

**Goal.** Convert Koda + Rex + Riko + Luna into core + skills. Then extend to the remaining 24 agents.
**Savings.** ~60–75% per hot agent; ~40% of total agent-preamble tokens across the roster.
**Ships.** Day 1–2.

**Files to create:**
- `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` — CLI: `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs <agent.md> [--dry-run|--staging|--write]`
- `scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs` — split rules (below)
- `scripts/compactor/render.mjs` — emits core body + skill files + updated frontmatter
- `scripts/compactor/README.md` — one-pager
- `~/.claude/skills/<agent>/*.md` — output skills

**Files to modify.** None in P1; script is standalone. Uses `fs.writeFileSync` with `.tmp` + `renameSync` (same pattern as `atomicWriteText` in [src/server.js:237](src/server.js#L237)).

**Heuristics (applied in order; stop when body ≤ budget):**

1. **H1 — Fenced on-demand sections.** `## Section` with heading matching `/^##\s+(billing|auth|migration|testing|deployment|debugging|design|stack-[a-z]+)/i` → extract to `skills/<agent>/<slug>.md`. Triggers = heading words + first-paragraph nouns.
2. **H2 — Protocol bloat.** Sections titled `PROTOCOL`, `DEEP PRE-BUILD PROTOCOL`, `CHECKLIST` > 100 lines → `skills/<agent>/protocol.md`. Keep 5-line summary + pointer.
3. **H3 — Example blocks.** Fenced ``` code blocks > 40 lines → `skills/<agent>/examples/<sha8>.md`. Replace with 2-line stub.
4. **H4 — Tool-specific guidance.** `### (Shopify|Supabase|Next\.?js|Stripe|Flutter|iOS)` → group by tool into `skills/<agent>/tools/<tool>.md`.
5. **H5 — Pattern catalogs.** 10+ numbered bullet patterns → `skills/<agent>/patterns.md`.
6. **H6 — Appendix / FAQ / antipatterns.** Post-`## Appendix|FAQ|Antipatterns` → `skills/<agent>/reference.md`.

**Always preserved in core:** frontmatter, `## Your Role`, `## Tier 1 first-load`, handoff contracts, the skill library block.

**Triggers for each split skill** are auto-indexed from (a) the section heading, (b) the first paragraph's nouns (stop-words removed), (c) any back-ticked identifiers in the first 10 lines.

**Verification:**
- `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ~/.claude/agents/koda.md --dry-run` prints before/after line counts + skill plan
- `--staging` writes to `./.compactor-staging/`; eyeball-diff before applying
- Post-`--write`: `wc -l ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` must show ≤ 400
- Real-task regression: one Koda task against old vs new body, diff outputs
- Global metric: `du -sh ~/.claude/agents` drops from ~1.8 MB to ~600 KB after all 28 compact

**Rollback.** `git restore` in `~/.claude`. Agent versioning table in SQLite already snapshots every save.

**Risk flags.**
- H3 may move trigger phrases that live inside examples. Mitigation: auto-index first 2 lines of every extracted block as additional triggers.
- Rex is an orchestrator; H2/H3 could break dispatch. **Special-case:** Rex gets `budget_lines: 700` and only H1/H5.
- Existing "MANDATORY load" blocks inside agents must NOT be touched in P1.

---

## PHASE 2 — Server lazy-load + frontmatter-only list

**Goal.** `/api/global/agents` returns metadata only; bodies fetched on demand from an in-process cache.
**Savings.** ~85% of the `/api/global/agents` payload (~1.7 MB → ~150 KB). Indirectly reduces any LLM that discovers agents via the API.
**Ships.** Day 3.

**Files to modify:**
- [src/server.js:250-270](src/server.js#L250-L270) (`parseAgent`) — add `parseAgentMeta(filePath)` that stops after frontmatter.
- [src/server.js:272-282](src/server.js#L272-L282) (`listAgents`) — add `listAgentsMeta(dir)` variant.
- [src/server.js:496-499](src/server.js#L496-L499) (`GET /api/global/agents`) — return meta only. Add `?full=1` escape hatch for backcompat (deprecation warning).
- [src/server.js:501-505](src/server.js#L501-L505) (`GET /api/global/agents/:name`) — wrap in cache.
- PUT handler (~line 507-518) — `agentCache.delete(filePath)` after atomic write.
- `client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx` — grep for `.body`; update if present (quick scan suggests it doesn't use `.body`).

**Cache layer.** In-process `Map<path, {mtimeMs, parsed}>`, mtime-invalidated. No Redis (overkill for <2 MB of hot data, would add a network hop and a dep).

```js
const agentCache = new Map();
function parseAgentCached(filePath) {
  const stat = fs.statSync(filePath);
  const hit = agentCache.get(filePath);
  if (hit && hit.mtimeMs === stat.mtimeMs) return hit.parsed;
  const parsed = parseAgent(filePath);
  agentCache.set(filePath, { mtimeMs: stat.mtimeMs, parsed });
  return parsed;
}
```

**API shapes:**

```
GET /api/global/agents
  → [{ filename, name, description, model, tools, category, department,
       lines, skills: [{id,triggers}], updatedAt }]    // no body, no raw

GET /api/global/agents/:name
  → full shape (as today) — cached

GET /api/global/agents/:name?meta=1
  → meta only

GET /api/global/agents?full=1
  → today's shape (30-day backcompat window)
```

**Verification.** `curl -s localhost:3847/api/global/agents | wc -c` before/after. AllAgents page load time in devtools. `/api/global/agents/koda` hits after warmup → cached (compare p50/p95).

**Rollback.** One-line revert; cache is additive.

**Risk.** Frontend might destructure `.body` somewhere. Grep `client/src` for `\.body\b` before shipping.

---

## PHASE 3 — Pre-write hook: guardrail on save

**Goal.** When an agent `.md` is saved, block/warn if over budget. Auto-suggests the compactor.
**Savings.** Prevents regression back to bloat. No direct token savings.
**Ships.** Day 4.

**Files to create:**
- `src/compactor/budget.js` — exports `checkBudget(agentObj)` → `{ok, violations, suggest}`.

**Files to modify:**
- PUT handler in [src/server.js](src/server.js) (~line 507-518) — budget check pre-write. On violation: `409 {error, budget, actual, suggestion}` unless `?force=1`. Keep atomic write + snapshot.

**Behavior:**
- ≤ 90% → `200 {ok:true}`
- 90–110% → `200 {ok:true, warning}`
- > 110% → `409 {error:"over_budget", runCompactor:"node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ..."}`
- `?force=1` → write anyway, set `compactor.allow_oversize: true` in FM

**Verification.** PUT a 5,000-line body → expect 409. PUT with `?force=1` → expect 200 and FM updated.

**Rollback.** `POLYGLOT_BUDGET_ENFORCE=0` env var short-circuits the check.

**Risk.** User saves a legit 500-line orchestrator and gets blocked. Mitigation: per-agent `budget_lines` override. Keep threshold generous; warn before reject.

---

## PHASE 4 — Golden-prompt regression harness

**Goal.** Prove the compactor didn't make agents dumber.
**Savings.** None directly — this is the safety net that lets P1 run aggressively.
**Ships.** Day 5–6.

**v1 (now) — diff + manual approve.** Staging-path write; human reviews diff. 80/20.
**v2 (defer) — automated LLM-judge scoring.** Only build if v1 reveals regressions.

**Files to create:**
- `tests/golden/<agent>/prompts.json` — 5–10 prompts per hot agent (Koda, Rex, Dato).

  ```json
  [{"id":"billing-checkout",
    "prompt":"Add Stripe checkout to /pricing",
    "expect_keywords":["stripe","webhook","price_id","success_url"],
    "must_mention_skill":"billing"}]
  ```

- `scripts/compactor/golden-run.mjs` — runs each prompt against OLD and NEW bodies, compares.
- `scripts/compactor/score.mjs` — scoring.

**Files to modify.** `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` — add `--with-golden` flag that runs harness before writing.

**Drift metric (v1, cheap):**
1. **Keyword recall.** `expect_keywords` present in NEW response must be ≥ 90% of OLD's recall.
2. **Skill-load check.** If prompt should trigger skill X, NEW must `Read` that path (grep tool-call log).
3. **Length ratio.** `new/old` ∈ [0.6, 1.4]. Outside → flag.
4. **No embedding similarity in v1.** Too expensive, too fuzzy. Revisit only if (1)–(3) miss real regressions.

**Pass threshold.** All 3 gates green on ≥ 80% of prompts per agent. Fail → staging file stays, real file untouched, diff rendered to `./.compactor-staging/<agent>.diff.html`.

**Verification.** Run against already-compacted Koda → expect all green. Intentionally break a skill trigger → expect red.

**Rollback.** Golden tests are read-only. Disable by not passing `--with-golden`.

**Risk flags.**
- Running prompts costs real tokens. **Mitigation:** cache OLD responses by (body-hash, prompt-hash); re-run NEW only. One-time cost ~$2–5 per hot agent, then $0.
- Flaky LLM outputs. **Mitigation:** temperature=0; run NEW twice; require both to pass.

---

## Sequencing & go/no-go

| Day | Phase | Expected tokens saved | Reversible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | P1 on Koda + Rex | ~30% global | yes (git) |
| 2 | P1 on remaining 26 | +15% global | yes |
| 3 | P2 server lazy-load | +85% list API | trivial |
| 4 | P3 pre-write hook | prevents regression | env flag |
| 5–6 | P4 golden tests | confidence | additive |

**Stop conditions.** If P1 on Koda regresses real tasks (measured by re-running 3 real prompts), halt, fix heuristics, don't touch other agents. Budget 1 day for heuristic tuning after Koda.

## Anti-over-engineering decisions

- **No Redis** — Map is enough for <2 MB of hot data.
- **No LLM compactor in v1** — deterministic is cheaper, reversible, testable.
- **No embedding similarity in v1** — keyword recall catches 90% of real regressions.
- **No MEMORY.md refactor** — user explicitly deferred.
- **No DB schema change** — frontmatter YAML is sufficient.
- **Kept existing versioning system** — don't replace what works.

|---|---|

| `scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs` | NEW — split rules |
| `scripts/compactor/render.mjs` | NEW — emits core + skills |
| `src/compactor/budget.js` | NEW (P3) — budget checker |

| [~/.claude/agents/koda.md](~/.claude/agents/koda.md) | Compacted in P1 |
| [~/.claude/agents/rex.md](~/.claude/agents/rex.md) | Compacted in P1 (special-case) |
| `~/.claude/skills/<agent>/*.md` | Generated by P1 |
| `tests/golden/<agent>/prompts.json` | NEW (P4) — regression prompts |

2. **P1 Koda.** `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ~/.claude/agents/koda.md --dry-run` → inspect plan. Then `--write`. Re-run `wc -l` → Koda ≤ 400.

4. **P2 API.** `curl -s localhost:3847/api/global/agents | wc -c` before/after. Expect >80% shrink.
5. **P2 cache.** `curl localhost:3847/api/global/agents/koda` twice; second call should be sub-ms (log instrumentation).

# Agent Context-Compactor — 4-Phase Plan

## Context

The user burns the $200/mo Claude subscription too fast. Audit shows the agent `.md` bodies are the primary driver of per-run token cost:

- 28 agents total. **Koda: 5,206 lines / 192 KB. Rex: 3,598 / 140 KB. Riko: 3,541 / 139 KB. Luna: 2,887 / 120 KB.** These four alone account for ~50% of global agent preamble.
- Mandatory per-run preamble (CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md + 2 pattern files + 3 Tier 1 files) is ~160 KB ≈ 40k tokens ≈ $0.12 *before any work starts*.
- Polyglot server reads full agent bodies on every request; no cache, no lazy-load, no body truncation. [src/server.js:250-270, 496-505](src/server.js).

The Claude Agent SDK loads the agent `.md` body into the system prompt at dispatch — that body **must shrink**. The SDK can't lazy-load at runtime, but the *LLM reading the body can* — if the core tells it to `Read` a skill file when keywords trigger (same mechanism the existing "MANDATORY load" blocks already use successfully).

**Design decision: deterministic Node script, not an LLM-driven agent.** Phase 1 runs at zero token cost, is testable, and reversible via git. LLM-assisted refinement is an explicit Phase 4 escape hatch only if heuristics plateau.

**Impact ranking:** P1 (core+skills split) recovers ~70% per hot agent. P2 (server lazy-list) cuts the `/api/global/agents` payload by ~85%. P3 (pre-write hook) prevents regression. P4 (golden tests) is insurance that lets P1 run aggressively.

---

## Skill-reference syntax (the contract the LLM reads)

Inserted at the bottom of every compacted core body:

```markdown
## Skill Library (load on demand)
When the user's task mentions keywords in the `triggers` list below, FIRST call
`Read` on the corresponding skill file, THEN proceed. Do not guess — load it.

- billing, subscription, stripe, checkout → ~/.claude/skills/koda/billing.md
- auth, login, session, rls → ~/.claude/skills/koda/auth.md
- migration, schema, rls policy → (DELEGATE to Dato, do not load)
- debugging, error loop → ~/.claude/skills/koda/debug-protocol.md
```

Machine-readable manifest in frontmatter (used by hook + tests, ignored by SDK):

```yaml
skills:
  - id: billing
    path: skills/koda/billing.md
    triggers: [billing, subscription, stripe, checkout, pricing]
    lines: 412
  - id: auth
    path: skills/koda/auth.md
    triggers: [auth, login, session, rls]
    lines: 287
compactor:
  version: 1
  budget_lines: 400
  budget_chars: 16000
  last_compacted: 2026-04-15T00:00:00Z
  original_sha: <sha of pre-compact body>
```

## Budget

| Agent class | Budget (lines) | Chars | Est. tokens | Override |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | 400 | 16,000 | ~4,500 | — |
| Orchestrator (Rex, Arya) | 700 | 28,000 | ~7,500 | `budget_lines: 700` |
| Lightweight (Vex, Zeph) | 300 | 12,000 | ~3,200 | — |

Over-budget = `body_lines > budget_lines` OR `body_chars > budget_chars`. Hook warns at 90%, rejects at 110% unless FM has `compactor.allow_oversize: true`.

---

## PHASE 1 — Deterministic core+skills splitter

**Goal.** Convert Koda + Rex + Riko + Luna into core + skills. Then extend to the remaining 24 agents.
**Savings.** ~60–75% per hot agent; ~40% of total agent-preamble tokens across the roster.
**Ships.** Day 1–2.

**Files to create:**
- `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` — CLI: `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs <agent.md> [--dry-run|--staging|--write]`
- `scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs` — split rules (below)
- `scripts/compactor/render.mjs` — emits core body + skill files + updated frontmatter
- `scripts/compactor/README.md` — one-pager
- `~/.claude/skills/<agent>/*.md` — output skills

**Files to modify.** None in P1; script is standalone. Uses `fs.writeFileSync` with `.tmp` + `renameSync` (same pattern as `atomicWriteText` in [src/server.js:237](src/server.js#L237)).

**Heuristics (applied in order; stop when body ≤ budget):**

1. **H1 — Fenced on-demand sections.** `## Section` with heading matching `/^##\s+(billing|auth|migration|testing|deployment|debugging|design|stack-[a-z]+)/i` → extract to `skills/<agent>/<slug>.md`. Triggers = heading words + first-paragraph nouns.
2. **H2 — Protocol bloat.** Sections titled `PROTOCOL`, `DEEP PRE-BUILD PROTOCOL`, `CHECKLIST` > 100 lines → `skills/<agent>/protocol.md`. Keep 5-line summary + pointer.
3. **H3 — Example blocks.** Fenced ``` code blocks > 40 lines → `skills/<agent>/examples/<sha8>.md`. Replace with 2-line stub.
4. **H4 — Tool-specific guidance.** `### (Shopify|Supabase|Next\.?js|Stripe|Flutter|iOS)` → group by tool into `skills/<agent>/tools/<tool>.md`.
5. **H5 — Pattern catalogs.** 10+ numbered bullet patterns → `skills/<agent>/patterns.md`.
6. **H6 — Appendix / FAQ / antipatterns.** Post-`## Appendix|FAQ|Antipatterns` → `skills/<agent>/reference.md`.

**Always preserved in core:** frontmatter, `## Your Role`, `## Tier 1 first-load`, handoff contracts, the skill library block.

**Triggers for each split skill** are auto-indexed from (a) the section heading, (b) the first paragraph's nouns (stop-words removed), (c) any back-ticked identifiers in the first 10 lines.

**Verification:**
- `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ~/.claude/agents/koda.md --dry-run` prints before/after line counts + skill plan
- `--staging` writes to `./.compactor-staging/`; eyeball-diff before applying
- Post-`--write`: `wc -l ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` must show ≤ 400
- Real-task regression: one Koda task against old vs new body, diff outputs
- Global metric: `du -sh ~/.claude/agents` drops from ~1.8 MB to ~600 KB after all 28 compact

**Rollback.** `git restore` in `~/.claude`. Agent versioning table in SQLite already snapshots every save.

**Risk flags.**
- H3 may move trigger phrases that live inside examples. Mitigation: auto-index first 2 lines of every extracted block as additional triggers.
- Rex is an orchestrator; H2/H3 could break dispatch. **Special-case:** Rex gets `budget_lines: 700` and only H1/H5.
- Existing "MANDATORY load" blocks inside agents must NOT be touched in P1.

---

## PHASE 2 — Server lazy-load + frontmatter-only list

**Goal.** `/api/global/agents` returns metadata only; bodies fetched on demand from an in-process cache.
**Savings.** ~85% of the `/api/global/agents` payload (~1.7 MB → ~150 KB). Indirectly reduces any LLM that discovers agents via the API.
**Ships.** Day 3.

**Files to modify:**
- [src/server.js:250-270](src/server.js#L250-L270) (`parseAgent`) — add `parseAgentMeta(filePath)` that stops after frontmatter.
- [src/server.js:272-282](src/server.js#L272-L282) (`listAgents`) — add `listAgentsMeta(dir)` variant.
- [src/server.js:496-499](src/server.js#L496-L499) (`GET /api/global/agents`) — return meta only. Add `?full=1` escape hatch for backcompat (deprecation warning).
- [src/server.js:501-505](src/server.js#L501-L505) (`GET /api/global/agents/:name`) — wrap in cache.
- PUT handler (~line 507-518) — `agentCache.delete(filePath)` after atomic write.
- `client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx` — grep for `.body`; update if present (quick scan suggests it doesn't use `.body`).

**Cache layer.** In-process `Map<path, {mtimeMs, parsed}>`, mtime-invalidated. No Redis (overkill for <2 MB of hot data, would add a network hop and a dep).

```js
const agentCache = new Map();
function parseAgentCached(filePath) {
  const stat = fs.statSync(filePath);
  const hit = agentCache.get(filePath);
  if (hit && hit.mtimeMs === stat.mtimeMs) return hit.parsed;
  const parsed = parseAgent(filePath);
  agentCache.set(filePath, { mtimeMs: stat.mtimeMs, parsed });
  return parsed;
}
```

**API shapes:**

```
GET /api/global/agents
  → [{ filename, name, description, model, tools, category, department,
       lines, skills: [{id,triggers}], updatedAt }]    // no body, no raw

GET /api/global/agents/:name
  → full shape (as today) — cached

GET /api/global/agents/:name?meta=1
  → meta only

GET /api/global/agents?full=1
  → today's shape (30-day backcompat window)
```

**Verification.** `curl -s localhost:3847/api/global/agents | wc -c` before/after. AllAgents page load time in devtools. `/api/global/agents/koda` hits after warmup → cached (compare p50/p95).

**Rollback.** One-line revert; cache is additive.

**Risk.** Frontend might destructure `.body` somewhere. Grep `client/src` for `\.body\b` before shipping.

---

## PHASE 3 — Pre-write hook: guardrail on save

**Goal.** When an agent `.md` is saved, block/warn if over budget. Auto-suggests the compactor.
**Savings.** Prevents regression back to bloat. No direct token savings.
**Ships.** Day 4.

**Files to create:**
- `src/compactor/budget.js` — exports `checkBudget(agentObj)` → `{ok, violations, suggest}`.

**Files to modify:**
- PUT handler in [src/server.js](src/server.js) (~line 507-518) — budget check pre-write. On violation: `409 {error, budget, actual, suggestion}` unless `?force=1`. Keep atomic write + snapshot.

**Behavior:**
- ≤ 90% → `200 {ok:true}`
- 90–110% → `200 {ok:true, warning}`
- > 110% → `409 {error:"over_budget", runCompactor:"node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ..."}`
- `?force=1` → write anyway, set `compactor.allow_oversize: true` in FM

**Verification.** PUT a 5,000-line body → expect 409. PUT with `?force=1` → expect 200 and FM updated.

**Rollback.** `POLYGLOT_BUDGET_ENFORCE=0` env var short-circuits the check.

**Risk.** User saves a legit 500-line orchestrator and gets blocked. Mitigation: per-agent `budget_lines` override. Keep threshold generous; warn before reject.

---

## PHASE 4 — Golden-prompt regression harness

**Goal.** Prove the compactor didn't make agents dumber.
**Savings.** None directly — this is the safety net that lets P1 run aggressively.
**Ships.** Day 5–6.

**v1 (now) — diff + manual approve.** Staging-path write; human reviews diff. 80/20.
**v2 (defer) — automated LLM-judge scoring.** Only build if v1 reveals regressions.

**Files to create:**
- `tests/golden/<agent>/prompts.json` — 5–10 prompts per hot agent (Koda, Rex, Dato).

  ```json
  [{"id":"billing-checkout",
    "prompt":"Add Stripe checkout to /pricing",
    "expect_keywords":["stripe","webhook","price_id","success_url"],
    "must_mention_skill":"billing"}]
  ```

- `scripts/compactor/golden-run.mjs` — runs each prompt against OLD and NEW bodies, compares.
- `scripts/compactor/score.mjs` — scoring.

**Files to modify.** `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` — add `--with-golden` flag that runs harness before writing.

**Drift metric (v1, cheap):**
1. **Keyword recall.** `expect_keywords` present in NEW response must be ≥ 90% of OLD's recall.
2. **Skill-load check.** If prompt should trigger skill X, NEW must `Read` that path (grep tool-call log).
3. **Length ratio.** `new/old` ∈ [0.6, 1.4]. Outside → flag.
4. **No embedding similarity in v1.** Too expensive, too fuzzy. Revisit only if (1)–(3) miss real regressions.

**Pass threshold.** All 3 gates green on ≥ 80% of prompts per agent. Fail → staging file stays, real file untouched, diff rendered to `./.compactor-staging/<agent>.diff.html`.

**Verification.** Run against already-compacted Koda → expect all green. Intentionally break a skill trigger → expect red.

**Rollback.** Golden tests are read-only. Disable by not passing `--with-golden`.

**Risk flags.**
- Running prompts costs real tokens. **Mitigation:** cache OLD responses by (body-hash, prompt-hash); re-run NEW only. One-time cost ~$2–5 per hot agent, then $0.
- Flaky LLM outputs. **Mitigation:** temperature=0; run NEW twice; require both to pass.

---

## Sequencing & go/no-go

| Day | Phase | Expected tokens saved | Reversible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | P1 on Koda + Rex | ~30% global | yes (git) |
| 2 | P1 on remaining 26 | +15% global | yes |
| 3 | P2 server lazy-load | +85% list API | trivial |
| 4 | P3 pre-write hook | prevents regression | env flag |
| 5–6 | P4 golden tests | confidence | additive |

**Stop conditions.** If P1 on Koda regresses real tasks (measured by re-running 3 real prompts), halt, fix heuristics, don't touch other agents. Budget 1 day for heuristic tuning after Koda.

## Anti-over-engineering decisions

- **No Redis** — Map is enough for <2 MB of hot data.
- **No LLM compactor in v1** — deterministic is cheaper, reversible, testable.
- **No embedding similarity in v1** — keyword recall catches 90% of real regressions.
- **No MEMORY.md refactor** — user explicitly deferred.
- **No DB schema change** — frontmatter YAML is sufficient.
- **Kept existing versioning system** — don't replace what works.

## Critical files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` | NEW — CLI entrypoint |
| `scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs` | NEW — split rules |
| `scripts/compactor/render.mjs` | NEW — emits core + skills |
| `src/compactor/budget.js` | NEW (P3) — budget checker |
| [src/server.js](src/server.js) lines 250-270, 496-518 | MODIFY (P2, P3) — parseAgentMeta, cache, lazy-list, PUT hook |
| [~/.claude/agents/koda.md](~/.claude/agents/koda.md) | Compacted in P1 |
| [~/.claude/agents/rex.md](~/.claude/agents/rex.md) | Compacted in P1 (special-case) |
| `~/.claude/skills/<agent>/*.md` | Generated by P1 |
| `tests/golden/<agent>/prompts.json` | NEW (P4) — regression prompts |

## Verification — end-to-end

1. **P1 baseline.** `wc -l ~/.claude/agents/*.md | tail -1` before. Record number.
2. **P1 Koda.** `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs ~/.claude/agents/koda.md --dry-run` → inspect plan. Then `--write`. Re-run `wc -l` → Koda ≤ 400.
3. **P1 real task.** Dispatch Koda with "add Dodo checkout to /pricing". Compare output (length, tool calls, final diff) against a pre-P1 run of the same prompt saved in `tests/golden/koda/billing-checkout.baseline.md`.
4. **P2 API.** `curl -s localhost:3847/api/global/agents | wc -c` before/after. Expect >80% shrink.
5. **P2 cache.** `curl localhost:3847/api/global/agents/koda` twice; second call should be sub-ms (log instrumentation).
6. **P3 hook.** `curl -X PUT localhost:3847/api/global/agents/koda -d @oversized.md` → expect 409.
7. **P4 harness.** `node scripts/compactor/golden-run.mjs koda` → expect all-green on compacted Koda.

input.content:
# Agent Compactor

Deterministic Node script that splits bloated agent `.md` files into a small **core** (loaded by the SDK on every dispatch) and a set of **on-demand skill files** (loaded by the LLM via `Read` when task keywords match).

## Why

Agent bodies grew to 3k–5k lines. The Claude Agent SDK loads the entire body into the system prompt at dispatch, so every run paid for all of it. A typical run was ~40k tokens of preamble before any work started. Compacting a 5,206-line Koda to a ~400-line core cuts that cost by 70–85% per run. Skills are loaded only when the task actually needs them.

## Quick start

```bash
# Dry-run (prints plan, no writes)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda

# Write to ./.compactor-staging/ for review
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --staging

# Apply to real paths (atomic)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write

# Every agent at once
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all              # dry-run
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write      # apply
```

## How it decides what to split

Six heuristics, applied in order, stopping when the body is under budget:

1. **H1 — topic sections** (`## Billing`, `## Auth`, etc.) → `skills/<agent>/<slug>.md`
2. **H2 — protocol bloat** (long `## Protocol`, `## Checklist`) → `skills/<agent>/…-protocol.md`
3. **H3 — large example blocks** (code fences > 40 lines) → `skills/<agent>/examples/<hash>.md`

## Why

Agent bodies grew to 3k–5k lines. The Claude Agent SDK loads the entire body into the system prompt at dispatch, so every run paid for all of it. ### Database Delegation (NEW — 2026-04-13)
For any task involving: schema design, migration creation, RLS policies, triggers, indexes, type generation, Realtime setup, Edge Functions, or database debugging → **delegate to Dato** (`~/.claude/agents/dato.md`).
Koda writes code that USES the database. Dato designs and maintains the database itself.
If Koda needs a new table or column, Koda tells Rex → Rex dispatches Dato → Dato creates migration + RLS + types → Dato hands back to Koda with ready-to-use types.

### DO NOT pre-load:
- `production-agent-mindset.md`, `autonomous-agent-protocol.md`, `universal-auto-fix-loop.md`, `universal-smart-defaults.md`, `validation-gates.md`, `quality-framework.md`, `saas-winning-patterns.md`, `competitive-dominance-engine.md`, `open-source-saas-patterns.md`, design KB files, etc.
- These contain useful reference material but loading them ALL before every task wastes context window and makes you WORSE at the actual task. Load them on-demand when you hit a specific situation they cover.

---
You are Koda, the Feature Builder agent for the Boldteq Software Factory.

## Your Role
You write all production code. Any feature, any stack, any complexity. You read the project's CLAUDE.md to understand the architecture, check memory for proven patterns, and build to production-grade quality every time. You validate input, check your own work before handoff, and ensure code is testable. You do not research, design architecture, write tests, or deploy.

---

## DEEP PRE-BUILD PROTOCOL (Run Before Every Single Task)
This is the most important section. Koda builds amazing features because it understands the task completely BEFORE writing a single character of code. Skipping this protocol produces mediocre code.
<!-- Full content moved to skills/koda/deep-pre-build-protocol-run-before-every-single-task.md -->

## Modern Stack Requirements (2025+)

Before writing any code, verify you're using current patterns:
- **React 19+:** Use `use()` hook for promises, `useOptimistic()` for optimistic updates, `useFormStatus()` for form states
- **Next.js 15+:** Server Components by default. Client Components only for: event handlers, hooks (useState/useEffect), browser APIs. Mark with `'use client'` — if you're marking more than 30% of components as client, you're doing it wrong
- **Server Actions:** Prefer `'use server'` async functions over API routes for mutations. API routes only for: webhooks, third-party integrations, non-Next.js clients
- **Suspense Boundaries:** Wrap every async Server Component with `<Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>`. Never show blank space while loading
- **Partial Pre-rendering (PPR):** For pages with mixed static/dynamic content, enable PPR in next.config. Static shell renders instantly, dynamic parts stream in
- **Streaming:** All AI responses stream. All large data fetches use streaming SSR. No blocking waterfalls
- **Tailwind v4:** Use CSS layers, `@theme` directive for design tokens. No `@apply` in component files — compose with utility classes
- **motion (formerly framer-motion):** Import from `motion/react` not `framer-motion`. Use `<motion.div>` for entrance animations, `AnimatePresence` for exit. Prefer CSS `@starting-style` for simple transitions
- **View Transitions API:** Use `document.startViewTransition()` for page navigation animations in supported browsers
- **Container Queries:** Use `@container` for component-level responsive design instead of only viewport media queries

## Production-Grade Execution Rules (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
<!-- 22 patterns moved to skills/koda/production-grade-execution-rules-non-negotiable-patterns.md -->

## Build Phases (Non-Negotiable Order)
